questions.text: List out the unique features of the town planning of the Indus-Saraswati Civilization.
questions.text_as_printed: List out the unique features of the town planning of the Indus-Saraswati Civilization. (A)

answer.value:
Urban Planning in Harappa:
The lower area was a residential zone.
Houses were built systematically.
Roads and drainage systems were constructed.
Houses had one or two stories.
Burnt bricks were used for construction.
House doors faced side lanes, with no windows facing the roads.
Wells and bathrooms were present in every house.
Domestic wastewater flowed into the drainage system, with manholes for cleaning and dedicated officials to oversee maintenance.

questions.text: Describe the social and political systems of the Vedic period.
questions.text_as_printed: Describe the social and political systems of the Vedic period. (A)

answer.value:
Vedic Period Social Structure:
Early Vedic Period:
The Rigveda's tenth mandala mentions the varna system.
Society had four varnas: Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras, determined by occupation.
Women held a high status, and marriage has practiced.
The king was called "Rajan," supported by institutions like Sabha, Samiti, and Vidhata.
Later Vedic Period:
The caste system became hereditary and more complex.
Women lost their social status, and practices like widow remarriage were banned.
Child marriage and dowry systems emerged.
The Vidhata institution disappeared, reducing the king's advisory bodies.

questions.text_as_printed: The people of the Indus–Saraswati Civilization were engaged in various crafts. Explain. (D)

answer.value:
• The people of the Indus–Saraswati Civilization depended on agriculture and trade
• Wheat, barley, and pulses were their main crops
• Hunting and fishing were widely practiced
• They cultivated cotton and made various kinds of clothes
• They were engaged in rearing animals like humped bull, cow, buffalo, sheep, goat, and hen
• Bulls were used for carrying loads
• Along with agriculture, trade and commerce held an important place
• Cities traded with rural areas as well as foreign regions
• Baluchistan, Saurashtra, and the Deccan regions were some of them
• They also had economic relations with the Mesopotamian Civilization.
